title: Kernel Queue Graffiti — Weekly Briefing
content:
Weekly notes from the kernel/queue workgroup — cadence: Thu sync + async followups. This week focused on 1) a small landing for the queue-time micro-allocator, 2) a shadow run of the soft-prefill sampler, and 3) a throttle tweak for gentle-batcher. High-level: incremental wins, some odd tail regressions still reproducible in synthetic bursts.

Attendees:
- Evelyn Park (owner)
- Mateo Ruiz (kernel)
- Priya Anand (prefill + cache)
- Liam Chen (bench + infra)
- Jordan Blake (oncall rotation)
- ran quick 20m deep-dive with Aaron (SRE) for deployment gating

Quick status bullets (what changed this week):
- Queue micro-allocator (PR 1248) landed on staging; reduces per-request queue metadata allocs by ~68% in the p99 path (local perf runs). Will monitor memory churn on longer runs.
- Shadow sampler v2 (soft-prefill) executed against 48h traffic window: improved effective KV hit-rate for conversational workloads by +4.8% median, but produced increased coalescing misses for very short seq requests (<=8 tokens).
- Gentle-batcher throttle change (reduce aggressive window) rolled to canary; observed reduced 95th latency spikes during a synthetic spike test (95th down ~12ms), but throughput impact at 90th percentile was -3% — acceptable for now.
- Kernel scheduling tweak (tickless batching) introduced subtle CPU scheduling jitter on older instance types; flagged and reverted on those nodes.

Metrics snapshot (synthetic bench + small prod sample):
- median batch size (hosted dev) => 4.1 -> 5.6 (after sampler change)
- KV cache hit-rate (shadow) => 72.6% -> 77.4% (median sessions)
- p95 latency (generation, 512 context) => 118ms -> 106ms on canary (with throttle applied)
- CPU steal events increased on m-older nodes by ~1.4x during tickless test

Notable observations / oddities:
- The sampler change increases cross-request coalescing for mid-length requests but slightly harms ultra-short requests. Hypothesis: soft-prefill increases prefix overlap windows which pushes tiny requests out of tight micro-batches.
- Memory churn drop from allocator patch is visible in short runs, but longer soak shows episodic spikes when eviction interacts with thinstate slots. Need night-long soak.
- Reproducer for tail jitter: synthetic client issuing 3-8 token requests at high QPS causes batch-splitting thrash under the new coalescer heuristics. Reproduced locally with workload harness; next is to test with KV shadow enabled.

Decisions made:
- Keep gentle-batcher throttle on canary for another week; extend canary to include two additional customers to validate production variance. Owner: Mateo.
- Roll forward micro-allocator to more staging pools (no canary poll) — because rollback is fast and memory wins are clear. Owner: Evelyn.
- Revert tickless scheduling on older nodes; keep active on latest instance families after additional kernel-level profiling. Owner: Liam.

Open action items (who / what / ETA):
- Priya: Run 48h shadow sampler soak with KV shadow enabled and produce failure-mode log extract (ETA: 2026-04-20).
- Mateo: Add deterministic trace points in allocator to capture ephemeral slot ownership on GC events (ETA: 2026-04-19).
- Liam: Night soak on staging for allocator + eviction interactions; capture heap flame graphs (start: 2026-04-16 night-run).
- Jordan: Prepare oncall runbook addendum for the new canary throttle behavior (ETA: 2026-04-18).
- Evelyn: Draft short postmortem if tail jitter reproduces in prod (condition-based) and coordinate rollback plan.

Follow-up experiments to schedule:
- 'Tiny-request fast-path' A/B: route <=8 token requests through a lightweight coalescer to test if we can avoid mis-binning caused by soft-prefill. Low-risk experiment; needs infra feature flagging. (Owner: Mateo + infra)
- 'Adaptive KV eviction bias': temporarily favor preserving recent conversation prefixes in shadow runs to see if hit-rate gains can be kept without raising eviction spikes. (Owner: Priya)
- 'Batch-splitting backpressure' probe: small client harness test that gradually increases QPS with short spikes to map the splitting threshold. Collect per-kernel queue histograms. (Owner: Liam)

Meeting notes / rough transcript highlights:
- Priya: "We saw the hit-rate lift where it matters — multi-turn chat — but the tiny single-turns got noisier."
- Mateo: "Allocator patch seems safe but I want the trace points before broad rollout — the episodic GC pattern worries me."
- Liam: "Tickless gave us lower nominal latency in microbench but revealed OS scheduling pathology on old instances; we need to target instance families for this feature."
- Jordan: "Oncall needs clear indicators to roll back throttle — we should add a query param to flip behavior immediately."

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Is there a way to bias coalescer to prefer prefix-similar requests when estimated latency budget < 40ms? (sketch: cheap simhash + count)
- Can we surface per-request 'micro-affinity' in traces so engineers can see why two requests were coalesced (or not)?
- How expensive is enabling KV-shadow end-to-end in long soaks (cost constraints)? Need SRE numbers.

Links / references used in sync:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1248 (allocator)
- Issue: ENG-4321 (shadow sampler parity)
- Benchmark harness: https://git.internal/redwood/bench/harness (private)

Closing thoughts: incremental, pragmatic wins. Focus next week on stabilizing the allocator on long soaks and narrowing the tail-jitter repro to a minimal harness. Keep canary conservative for throttle. Aim to move the tiny-request fast-path from idea -> feature-flagged experiment next sprint.

Quick TODO (short checklist):
- [ ] Night soak (Liam)
- [ ] Trace points in allocator (Mateo)
- [ ] KV-shadow 48h (Priya)
- [ ] Oncall addendum (Jordan)
- [ ] Feature flag for tiny-request fast-path (Evelyn + infra)

End of briefing.
